config.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface

intro.title: PropTypes / TypeScript Interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that displays user information, such as a name and age. You will learn how to use PropTypes to define and validate the expected data types for the component's props, ensuring your component receives the correct information. This introduces the core concept of type checking in JavaScript, which helps catch errors early and makes your code more reliable. By the end, you'll understand how PropTypes improve component robustness and developer experience in React applications.
intro.usecase: In real-world React applications, PropTypes and TypeScript interfaces are essential for building maintainable component libraries and design systems. For example, when creating a dashboard with reusable data visualization components like charts, tables, and filters, these type definitions ensure each component receives the correct data format and configuration props. This prevents runtime errors when different teams work on the same codebase, such as when a marketing team's analytics panel needs to integrate with an engineering team's performance monitoring widgets. By defining clear contracts for component props, developers can catch type mismatches during development rather than in production, saving debugging time and improving code reliability across complex applications like e-commerce platforms or financial dashboards.

objectives: Implement PropTypes to validate component props in a React application
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of component props
Construct reusable components with type-safe prop definitions
Configure PropTypes with both required and optional prop validations
Update existing components to include prop type checking
Integrate TypeScript interfaces with functional and class components
Manipulate complex prop structures using PropTypes and TypeScript

steps.title: Import React and PropTypes
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and PropTypes from 'prop-types'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the module name and the from keyword with the package name in quotes.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have imported React and PropTypes, making them available for use in your component.
successCriteria: React and PropTypes are imported from their respective packages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React from 'react' and PropTypes from 'prop-types'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. Remember to import React from 'react' and PropTypes from 'prop-types' using the import statement.

steps.title: Create a UserInfo component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named UserInfo that takes props as its parameter and returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to include the props parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: A UserInfo component is defined with props as its parameter and returns null.
successCriteria: The code defines a functional component named UserInfo that accepts props and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a component named UserInfo that takes props as a parameter and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you named it UserInfo, included props as a parameter, and returned null.

steps.title: Destructure props in the component
steps.instruction: Inside your UserInfo component, destructure the props parameter to extract name, age, and isActive values.
steps.hint: Use curly braces within the function parameters to extract specific properties from props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component parameters should now be destructured to directly access name, age, and isActive.
successCriteria: The UserInfo component has destructured props with name, age, and isActive extracted.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're destructuring all three properties: name, age, and isActive from the props parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to destructure the props parameter to extract name, age, and isActive.

steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns JSX that renders the user data values in the UI.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add PropTypes for name prop
steps.instruction: Add PropTypes validation to your UserInfo component to specify that the 'name' prop should be a string and is required.
steps.hint: Use PropTypes.string.isRequired to define that the name prop must be a string and must be provided.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserInfo component will have PropTypes validation that enforces the name prop as a required string.
successCriteria: PropTypes validation is added to UserInfo specifying name as PropTypes.string.isRequired.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some PropTypes validation, but make sure to specify that name is a string and required.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PropTypes validation for the name prop is missing or incorrect. It should be defined as a required string.

steps.title: Add PropTypes for age prop
steps.instruction: Add PropTypes validation for the age prop, specifying it should be a number and is required.
steps.hint: Add a prop type definition for age using PropTypes.number.isRequired.
steps.expectedOutcome: The age prop will be validated as a required number.
successCriteria: PropTypes validation for age is added as a required number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the age prop validation with PropTypes.number.isRequired.
steps.feedbackWrong: The age prop validation is missing or incorrect. It should be defined as a required number using PropTypes.number.isRequired.

steps.title: Add PropTypes for isActive prop
steps.instruction: Add PropTypes validation for the isActive prop, making it a boolean with a default value of false.
steps.hint: Use PropTypes.bool and set the default value using defaultProps.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UserInfo component will have PropTypes validation for isActive as a boolean with a default value of false.
successCriteria: isActive is defined in UserInfo.propTypes as PropTypes.bool and has a default value of false in UserInfo.defaultProps.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both the PropTypes validation for isActive as a boolean and set its default value to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added isActive to UserInfo.propTypes as PropTypes.bool and set its default value to false in UserInfo.defaultProps.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX.
steps.hint: Define a function called App that returns some JSX structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and ready to be used as the main component.
successCriteria: A functional component named App is created and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a function named App that returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a function called App with a return statement containing JSX.

steps.title: Render UserInfo with correct props
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, render the UserInfo component with the required props: name set to a string, age set to a number, and isActive set to a boolean.
steps.hint: Pass the props as attributes to the UserInfo component. For example: <UserInfo name="John" age={30} isActive={true} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will render the UserInfo component with all three props passed correctly.
successCriteria: UserInfo is rendered inside App with name, age, and isActive props provided as attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're passing all three required props (name, age, and isActive) to the UserInfo component. Check that age uses curly braces for the number value and isActive uses curly braces for the boolean.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UserInfo component isn't being rendered with the correct props. Remember to include all three props: name (string), age (number), and isActive (boolean) as attributes on the UserInfo component.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export.
steps.hint: Look for the export statement at the bottom of the file. The App component should be exported as default.
steps.analogousExample:
// Exporting a component as default
export default App;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The App component is exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're exporting the App component as the default export.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your export statement. You need to export the App component as default.
